video.title: Fantasy Basketball Auction Mock Draft/Salary Cap Mock Draft

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team, 9-category auction mock draft with a $200 budget and 13-man rosters, and gives his own price for each player as they go. The room starts hot. One manager pays $80 each for Victor Wembanyama and Nikola Jokic, and most top names go above his prices. Luka Doncic at $61 is the main early bargain. Josh skips the stars and builds a balanced team from mid-tier players, including Dyson Daniels, Deni Avdija, LaMelo Ball, Brandon Miller, Trey Murphy and Paolo Banchero. Late in the draft, cheap players keep going for $3 to $8, and no player goes for $1 until about pick 124. Real bargains like Derrick White and Norman Powell slip through when managers run low on money. Projections put Cayenne's team first and Josh's a very close second. He warns that paying top prices for two stars leaves no margin for error.

rules.text: Auction prices change whenever league settings, team count or roster size change. His valuations will be different from what happens in your league.
rules.quote: Reminder, as soon as things in an auction draft change, the prices will change.

rules.text: Nominate a mid or low-tier player first to see how the room values players like that, instead of opening with big names.
Nominating big names early gets cash off the board. Early prices tell you whether the room is hot or cold.
rules.quote: Again, the idea of getting cash off the board is an important one.

rules.text: He tries to keep his top-end prices low when setting values for elite players.
rules.quote: I again tried to suppress the top end prices when I'm thinking about it.

rules.text: Paying $80 each for two superstars is too much to win the league, even if they are elite.
rules.quote: You're not winning at that price. That's just that's too difficult to do.

rules.text: In a hot room, wait for bargains and target mid-round value rather than paying full price at the top.
rules.quote: It's not really sitting bargain for me. And in a in a hot room, I want a bit of a bargain.

rules.text: A hot room pushes him toward a cheaper, balanced build.
rules.quote: hot room. So, I'm now I am locking in on a on a

rules.text: Being a fan of a player does not mean getting him at any cost. Only pay up to his value.
rules.quote: that is not acquire at all costs. That is just get where the value sits

rules.text: To do well in an auction, you have to be comfortable not owning a first-round player.
rules.quote: you can be comfortable not having a first round type player.

rules.text: If an opponent is about to overpay in a way that hurts him for the rest of the draft, let him have the player instead of fighting.
rules.quote: I thought Eric was going to over bid on someone and it puts him at a real disadvantage rest of the draft.

rules.text: Keep track of how much you can spend per open slot, holding back money for $1 bench slots.
rules.quote: If I take my two $1 slots, that's five for 70. So, 14 bucks a slot.

rules.text: Late in a hot draft, real value appears if you have the patience to wait.
rules.quote: This is where the value is is really coming in. If you've got the balls and the patience

rules.text: Nominate players you see as $1 guys early. Others will often overpay $4 or $5 for them.
rules.quote: Get some $1 guys out early and they go for like four

rules.text: How the market reacts to an injury tag can leave value on the board.
rules.quote: how are people going to react to the injury? because sometimes that might just leave value.

rules.text: Leave yourself a $1 streaming slot. Finishing with unused money means you planned your budget wrong.
rules.quote: I don't like the strategy of not having a $1 player

rules.text: Late in the draft, track each manager's max bid. Someone holding money can snipe the player you are waiting on.
rules.quote: Tatum and Strangers are my things here. So, as soon as Keegan goes up, I'm going to get cooked here.

rules.text: You can build a good team around two high-priced stars, but there is no margin for error. If one is out, the team loses that week.
rules.quote: You can build a a good team with the two guys at high prices. You have just no margin for error.
